title: Short Corner Overload Structure
definition: A structured short corner routine that uses wide numerical overloads to stretch the defense and create central penetration or shooting opportunities.
content: This tactical approach replaces traditional aerial deliveries with a flexible, possession-based setup designed to disrupt defensive organization. The structure typically involves nine players: two near the ball-taker (one on the goal line) to force extra defensive coverage, three circulating around the box perimeter, and four positioned inside the penalty area. This arrangement creates a defensive dilemma, as opponents cannot simultaneously maintain central strength and cover wide passing options. The primary objective is to exploit the resulting defensive disorganization through three avenues: quick combination play along the sideline to generate superior crossing angles, opportunistic shots from the top of the box as attention shifts wide, and tempo control by a creative playmaker to recycle possession until favorable angles emerge. The method blurs the line between set pieces and open play, requiring players to maintain decision-making flexibility rather than committing to a predetermined outcome. If the defense crowds the short option, space opens elsewhere; if they commit minimally, the team progresses into vulnerable areas. This strategy relies on constant repositioning by defenders to create momentary gaps for attackers to exploit.

source.name: FIFA Training Centre: Short corners: structure and decision-making in Chelsea's set plays
